profile.reading:
This OpenStreetMap record, tagged Aligned Energy Data Center, sits at coordinates that correspond closely to 2500 West Union Hills Drive in Phoenix, Arizona, the 55 acre campus address Aligned's own Phoenix location page lists for its cluster of buildings there, referenced in company materials as the PHX-01, PHX-02, and PHX-03 group. Aligned's own site discloses campus-level infrastructure standards for this Union Hills location, including a Tier III design approach with 3 megawatt generators and 2 megawatt uninterruptible power supply units per building in an N+1 block redundant topology, 500 kVA power distribution units, and 415 volt distribution to the rack, but it does not break out individual capacity or square footage figures per building on that page, and no dedicated press release matching this exact coordinate to one specific building code among PHX-01 through PHX-03 could be located this session. Given that ambiguity, no specific capacity, square footage, or building-code assignment beyond the general Union Hills campus location is claimed here.

Aligned's published cooling design for its current campuses, including this one, centers on what it calls Delta3 air cooling arrays housed in dedicated mechanical galleries, with secondary loops supporting DeltaFlow liquid cooling meant for GPU intensive workloads, running on a closed loop chilled water system built with N+1 redundancy. That combination, air cooling for general IT load plus a liquid loop reserved for dense GPU racks, is the kind of retrofit path colocation operators are adding to existing halls to host AI accelerator hardware without redesigning the whole building around liquid cooling. Aligned lists SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, HITECH, NIST 800-53, and ISO 27001 as certifications carried across its facilities, along with a 100 percent uptime service level commitment, though again the company's own materials describe these as standards applied across its portfolio rather than figures unique to this specific building.

A separate Aligned facility in the Phoenix market, PHX-06, is a distinct building from this Union Hills campus and should not be conflated with it. Aligned's July 2025 press release states PHX-06 earned Three Green Globes for New Construction from the Green Building Initiative, citing 100 percent renewable power, reduced water use, and what Aligned calls Adaptive Modular Infrastructure, prefabricated standardized modules meant to cut construction waste and emissions. Aligned's chief executive Andrew Schaap was quoted calling Aligned the highest certifying data center operator in that Green Globes program, though the press release itself does not give PHX-06's street address.

Aligned, formerly known as Aligned Energy, the name still reflected in this record's OpenStreetMap tag, describes its overall footprint today as more than fifty campuses and roughly five gigawatts of contracted and available capacity across the Americas, with Latin American operations run under the ODATA brand. Ownership has shifted substantially over the company's history, most recently with an October 2025 agreement for a consortium called AI Infrastructure Partnership, combining BlackRock Global Infrastructure Partners and MGX, to acquire all of Aligned's equity from majority owner Macquarie Asset Management and its co-investors in a deal valued near 40 billion dollars, with a close indicated around July 2026 in Aligned's own materials, though not independently confirmed by a dedicated press release this session.

reading.body:
This facility publishes 200,000 square feet of technical space but no power capacity figure, making it impossible to assess its relevance to AI infrastructure or compare it to other Arizona data centers.

The operator's press release describes a Phase II expansion with a planned 1.15 power usage effectiveness ratio and rack densities up to 50 kilowatts per unit. These specifications indicate high-density design appropriate for compute workloads. Without a published megawatt figure, however, this site cannot place the facility in Arizona's mapped inventory or determine whether it serves AI tenants versus other workloads.

Arizona has 56 tracked facilities, but only four publish power capacity. This facility joins a larger pattern where operator disclosure varies widely. Size in square footage does not predict power draw or compute density, because cooling approach, voltage delivery, and rack configuration differ across data centers. A reader evaluating this campus would require the operator to publish IT load in megawatts before making siting or investment decisions.

The parent company, Aligned Data Centers, operates 87 facilities across 51 campuses with stated 6.4 gigawatts of capacity and is undergoing a $40 billion ownership transfer. The Phoenix expansion alone claims up to 60 megawatts at full buildout. Publication of this site-level capacity would clarify whether Aligned's portfolio growth is concentrated in a few large campuses or distributed across many smaller ones, which matters for understanding whether grid constraints bind differently by region.
